What it means: The Boston City Council Committee on Education held a hearing on September 17, 2026 [00:55, 01:01], regarding student and family homelessness in Boston Public Schools [02:13, 04:29]. Participants reviewed data showing roughly one in ten BPS students experienced homelessness during the 2024 to 2025 school year [04:39], highlighting the negative impacts of housing instability on school attendance and student well-being [05:28, 1:55:30]. Discussions focused on expanding early identification through school liaisons [23:12, 38:57], strengthening legal aid and upstream eviction prevention in high-risk zip codes [49:08, 2:09:50], and maintaining wraparound support services despite the expiration of temporary grant and ESSER funding [29:04, 1:24:53].

Who moved it: The hearing matter was referred to the committee by Councilor Mejia [02:20], with Councilor Weber leading the effort as a primary sponsor [11:49, 14:22, 16:58]. Councilors Breadon [11:43], Flynn [18:35], and Fitzgerald [1:03:09] also participated and asked questions. Panelists presenting testimony included representatives from Boston Public Schools [19:46], the Office of Housing Stability [32:42], United Way [1:39:05], Higher Ground [1:45:03], Family Aid [1:54:48], and Greater Boston Legal Services [2:08:29].

What to watch: Watch how the city council and school leaders address the loss of federal ESSER funding for homeless student support programs [29:04, 1:24:53], including whether local funds will be allocated to replace the estimated 1.8 million dollar investment [1:26:15, 1:29:17]. Watch for further coordination between city housing officials and public housing authorities to scale up landlord-tenant mediation and eviction record sealing [1:15:17, 2:38:53]. The transcript does not record any formal committee votes during the session, and officials did not definitively settle whether a previously established family homelessness commission remains formally active [15:46, 55:45].

summary: The committee held a hearing to address student housing instability, family homelessness, and their impacts on Boston Public Schools [03:22], [04:49]. Participants examined rising rental costs and eviction risks facing families [12:06], [20:46], alongside the role of McKinney-Vento homeless liaisons and school social workers in identifying early warning indicators of housing hardship [07:55], [08:17], [39:38]. Panelists and officials reviewed current inter-agency efforts and supportive interventions, including the Housing Innovation Program [28:40], emergency financial assistance [32:51], legal representation to navigate eviction proceedings [2:08:45], and flexible funding models to keep children stably housed [1:43:02]. While no formal policy decisions or votes occurred, speakers emphasized the necessity of scaling upstream homelessness prevention strategies, improving family outreach, and expanding wrap-around housing supports across the city [1:41:08], [2:21:12], [2:39:47].
